anchor: Such bounds are service-level objectives (SLOs); following serving-systems usage, this document writes 'the evaluation SLA' for the specific tail bounds it grades every policy against, and SLO for the general concept.
claim_text: Service-level objectives (SLOs) are general bounds; the evaluation SLA refers to specific tail bounds graded against policies.

anchor: Meeting them economically on shared GPU fleets pushed serving from replicated monoliths toward disaggregation: prefill and decode in separate pools sized to their own bottlenecks
claim_text: Economically meeting SLOs on shared GPU fleets pushed serving toward disaggregation with prefill and decode in separate pools.

anchor: A multimodal request adds a third phase preceding both: a vision encoder, in current practice a Vision Transformer, ingests the request's images as grids of patches and emits embedding tokens.
claim_text: A multimodal request adds a vision encoder phase that ingests images as grids of patches and emits embedding tokens.

anchor: These properties invite modality disaggregation: run the encoder as its own pool, on its own hardware class, scaled independently.
claim_text: Modality disaggregation runs the encoder as its own pool on its own hardware class, scaled independently.

anchor: The prevailing practice, inherited from stateless web serving, is reactive: watch an aggregate load signal (request rate or a utilization average) and add or remove replicas at a threshold.
claim_text: The prevailing practice for scaling is reactive, watching an aggregate load signal and adding or removing replicas at a threshold.

anchor: Two assumptions hide in that loop — that the watched signal carries each pool's demand, and that new replicas arrive faster than the load changes.
claim_text: Reactive scaling assumes the watched signal carries each pool's demand and that new replicas arrive faster than load changes.

anchor: Prediction-driven capacity management has appeared for text-only LLM fleets — forecast-aware fleet planning, prewarming GPUs against forecast peak load — but watches aggregate, request-level signals
claim_text: Prediction-driven capacity management for text-only LLM fleets watches aggregate, request-level signals.

anchor: The position this document defends, stated compactly: In a modality-disaggregated multimodal serving system, no single load signal can size every pool
claim_text: In a modality-disaggregated multimodal serving system, no single load signal can size every pool.
